purpose: Chronological durable notebook for worker evolution: observed behavior, experiments, delays, tricks, failures and hypotheses. It complements binding contracts and receipts; it does not replace them.

evidence_classes.HISTORICAL_RECONSTRUCTION: Recovered from prior project conversations/files; useful but below current durable receipts.
evidence_classes.HUMAN_OBSERVATION: Human-reported behavior preserved as a hypothesis/input until externally reproduced.

entries.title: ZIP / Root Dispatcher era
entries.summary: Historical workflow used external chats as workers, the main chat as a Root Dispatcher, and the human as temporary transport for prompts/returns. Narrow missions and packaged ZIP/return artifacts were preferred over generic consultancy. The long-term intention was to automate the transport inside Prometeo.
entries.lesson: Human copy/paste is a transitional transport, not the target architecture. Keep worker missions narrow and returns integrable.
entries.evidence_boundary: Recovered project-history/file context; not proof of current runtime behavior.

entries.title: Worker Evolution Lab
entries.summary: CATLAB exploration used stage-specific variants and independent replicas. CATLAB-P2B confirmed V3_EVIDENCE_MAP and V4_TWO_PASS_REVIEW 3/3 each for primary+reallocation; V3 was promoted as baseline to avoid unconditional extra overhead.
entries.lesson: Change one stage rule at a time; completion/evidence outrank speed. Reproduce candidate laws before promotion.

entries.title: PARKED / early-exit failure mode
entries.summary: Earlier SWARM-era flows explicitly returned PARKED/WAIT states and many shells stopped early. The human repeatedly observed that worker-visible terminal vocabulary made it easy for a shell to stop rather than continue useful work.
entries.lesson: Do not use PARKED/ACTIVE as liveness. Present useful continuation as the normal path. Terminal language must correspond to a real durable boundary, not a convenient narrative exit.
entries.evidence_boundary: The durable current law is strong; the claimed psychological wording effect remains a human observation until reproduced experimentally.

entries.title: Large text batches kept workers producing
entries.summary: Historical grid experiments suggested that workers could continue producing substantial local text batches when the task itself remained concrete, rather than entering wait/parking behavior.
entries.lesson: Test local productive load as a residency tool, but do not confuse synthetic text with product value.
entries.evidence_boundary: Historical reconstruction; exact receipts for the older grid figures remain incomplete.

entries.title: LOCAL_CAPACITY_V2_10X
entries.summary: Nine recovered replicas completed the heterogeneous local batch, each around 2268–2548 output words. Workers reported zero external tools/reads/writes and no late-batch degradation; timing remained self-reported only. Two distinct conversations produced the same model-generated replica_id.
entries.lesson: Large local batches are promising; model-generated identity and self-reported clocks are not trustworthy authority.

entries.title: Worker Playbook distilled
entries.summary: Binding laws and experimental findings were distilled into a human+machine playbook covering fresh identity, local batching, external clocks, sparse writes, atomic ownership, deterministic sharding, resident 3/6/8, RUN vs POOL and evidence-map verification.
entries.lesson: Worker learning must be written back, not left inside the Guide/chat.

entries.title: Prerequisite gating bug
entries.summary: PRE-GUIDE critic/finalizer jobs became claimable before prerequisites were satisfied. Internal job instructions returned dependency boundaries instead of fabricating results, but capacity was wasted.
entries.lesson: Do not rely on the model to respect dependency order when the allocator can enforce it. Gate prerequisites below the worker interface.

entries.title: System-multiplier starvation
entries.summary: High-priority worker/runtime improvement jobs were READY but could be absent from the compact POOL frontier because product work filled the unified batch first.
entries.lesson: Keep product dominant while reserving a tiny bounded share for system multipliers, otherwise orchestration fixes can starve indefinitely.

entries.title: Explicit zero-ledger
entries.summary: Writing or mentally holding expected external_reads=0/external_writes=0/tool_calls=0 may reinforce instruction retention, but it is not security and self-reported zeros are not external measurement.
entries.lesson: Use zero-ledger as a prompting variant only; verify externally and never upgrade missing evidence to zero.

entries.title: Block review / continuation priming / fill-the-questions
entries.summary: Three candidate prompting techniques are under controlled comparison: silent review after each local block, explicit anti-early-answer continuation priming, and a PRE-GUIDE question scaffold that must be filled before return.
entries.lesson: These are interventions, not laws. Compare matched replicas and preserve one causal delta per variant.

entries.title: First 15 reported RUN launches produced no RUN evidence
entries.summary: The human reported launching 15 chats, while durable RUN status still showed zero RUN beacons and zero slot claims. Causal attribution was unknown, so the system stopped scaling instead of pretending those launches entered the benchmark.
entries.lesson: Human launch count is not slot occupancy. Admission must be measured from durable beacon+claim evidence.
entries.evidence_boundary: 15 launch attempts came from human report; durable observation was zero RUN beacons/claims at that checkpoint.

entries.title: Single RUN admission canary succeeded
entries.summary: Fresh worker wc-20260930T102900Z-d4a7c91e52bf created a RUN beacon, claimed S002 (V1_EXPLICIT_ZERO_LEDGER), reached the single B3 MIDPOINT, completed the 72-task primary with 3636 useful words, persisted the primary receipt and claimed paired reallocation R002.
entries.lesson: The previously unproven RUN admission path now works through primary return and entry into reallocation. The correct next move is parallel scale, not more sequential admission probing.

entries.title: Admission canary must not freeze the broader lab
entries.summary: A one-worker canary is appropriate when a previously broken transition is unproven. It should not pause unrelated parallel worker experiments, and once the failed transition is crossed, the frozen cohort should scale immediately.
entries.lesson: Use sequential canaries for unknown failure boundaries, not as the default experimental cadence.
entries.next_test: Run the remaining RESIDENCY-MACROBATCH slots in parallel and measure admission loss, variant completion, residency and reallocation.

open_questions: What macro-batch size maximizes useful work per external I/O before quality declines?
Which prompting variant improves completion/residency without increasing correction or evidence debt?
What is the externally observed distribution of claim→midpoint→primary→reallocation→close duration?
How much does wording change early termination independent of workload difficulty?
How many GitHub reads/writes occur per useful durable unit under macro-batching?
Can two independent worker analysts reliably prepare the Guide's human-facing answer?
What is the right admission-canary threshold before parallel scale for future RUNs?
authority_boundary: History/playbook projection only. No routing, scheduling, promotion or liveness authority.
